methods.label: Follow the parity of the next three terms
methods.explanation:
Let \(m=a_1\). If \(m\) is even, then \(a_2=m/2<m\), so every even starting value fails.

For odd \(m\), the next two terms are
\[
a_2=3m+1,\qquad a_3=\frac{3m+1}{2}.
\]
Both exceed \(m\), since \(m>0\). Thus only the comparison with \(a_4\) remains. Every positive odd integer has exactly one of the following forms, with a unique integer \(q\ge0\).

If \(m=4q+1\), then \(a_3=6q+2\) is even, so
\[
a_4=3q+1\le4q+1=m.
\]
This case fails, including \(q=0\), when equality occurs.

If \(m=4q+3\), then \(a_3=6q+5\) is odd, so
\[
a_4=3(6q+5)+1=18q+16>4q+3=m.
\]
Every starting value in this case succeeds.

The successful values are therefore exactly \(4q+3\le2008\). This holds for \(q=0,1,\ldots,501\), giving \(\boxed{502}\) distinct starting values, choice D. The even case and the two odd cases exhaust all positive integers.
